Package org.geysermc.paletter.internal.behaviour

Class Behaviour

java.lang.Object
org.geysermc.paletter.internal.behaviour.Behaviour
@Internal public final class Behaviour extends Object
The behaviour values of the blocks and items of one Palette, behind Palette.resolve(org.geysermc.paletter.vanilla.BedrockBlockState) and ResolvedItem.behaviour(). Thread safe.

Vanilla values come from the bundled captures of the palette's data version (an older capture's value when the version has none, see Provenance.inherited()); keys the captures lack fall back to what the component data BDS sends says (use duration of food, ...). Values come from BDS directly wherever possible (what BDS sends, Paletter's own captures) and from third-party dumps otherwise (Provenance.thirdParty()); sources that disagree without BDS evidence settling it are Provenance.disputed().

Custom blocks and items, and vanilla items a layer overrides, are read from the component data the palette sends for them, converted to the engine units of the key: e.g. minecraft:friction 0.4 is BlockBehaviour.FRICTION 0.6, minecraft:collision_box in pixels is a BlockShape in blocks. A custom block or item without the component gets BDS's default for the key, if it is known; else there is no value (Provenance.unknownDefault()).

Values are kept in dense columns, one per key (BehaviourKey.ordinal()), built the first time a key is asked for. The handles (BlockValues, ItemValues) are a behaviour and a position in its columns. A palette that extends another one (Palette.extend(org.geysermc.paletter.PaletteLayer)) has the other one's states first: their handles and columns are the other palette's (their values are the same), and only the states the layers added have columns here. A Provenance is only built by provenance(org.geysermc.paletter.block.RegisteredBlockState, org.geysermc.paletter.behaviour.BehaviourKey<?>) and explain(org.geysermc.paletter.block.RegisteredBlockState, org.geysermc.paletter.behaviour.BehaviourKey<?>).
